title: Two-Stage Rolling Resilient Dispatch of Port Micro-Energy Grid Clusters Considering Spatio-Temporal Transfer of Hydrogen-Powered Vessels under Typhoon Conditions
author: Liu, Jia and Liang, Ruqin and Tang, Zao and Su, Tong and Chen, Yuhao and Zeng, Pingliang and Long, Chao
source: Google Scholar export supplied by Tong Su, 2026-10-01
abstractSource: <jats:p>To enhance the resilience of coordinated dispatch in port micro-energy grid (PMEG) clusters under typhoon conditions, this paper develops a two-stage rolling resilient dispatch strategy that explicitly considers the spatio-temporal transfer of hydrogen-powered vessels. A typhoon-driven scenario model first maps the evolving wind field into wind-power availability, port-load corrections, external-grid support limits, and maritime route-accessibility conditions. Hydrogen-powered vessels are then represented as mobile hydrogen-storage and emergency ship-to-grid (S2G) resources in a time-expanded network, where navigation bans, wind-induced speed reduction, sailing energy consumption, berthing, refueling, and S2G constraints are jointly enforced. In the pre-disaster stage, unit commitment, port and vessel hydrogen preparation, vessel pre-deployment, and a forecast-feasible baseline sailing-operating schedule are determined from forecast information. In the intra-disaster stage, port electricity-hydrogen dispatch, vessel transfer, S2G support, and load curtailment are re-optimized in a receding-horizon manner using updated meteorological and operating states. After the physical schedule is finalized, an ex-post asymmetric Nash bargaining mechanism allocates the cooperative benefit among ports, preserving the coordinated dispatch while ensuring individual rationality. Case studies demonstrate the value of combining advance preparation, typhoon-constrained vessel mobility, and ex-post settlement for resilient multi-port operation.</jats:p>
